title: Device-bound token rotation — personal notes
content:
Context:
Quick personal sketch for a device-bound token rotation flow for edge clients (mobile and small on-prem agents) that call Redwood’s inference API. Goal is to minimize blast radius when devices are compromised, keep UX friction low, and support both offline-limited devices and always-online ones.

Key constraints:
- Devices have intermittent connectivity.
- Many devices are untrusted (end-user devices), some are semi-trusted (company-managed).
- We need low-latency token check on request path — cannot block on heavy crypto every call.
- Support private deployments (VPC) and hosted API modes.
- Integrate with KMS/HSM for key material rotation on server side.

High-level choices considered:
1) Long-lived device token + server-side revocation list (fast checks but large revocation lists).
2) Short-lived JWT signed by authority + refresh token pattern (classic OAuth).
3) Mutual TLS with device certificate and CRL/OCSP checks (strong, but heavy for many devices).
4) Attestation-backed ephemeral tokens (TPM/TEE) for managed devices.

Quick take: prefer short-lived signed tokens (option 2) with asymmetric rotation and per-device refresh keys for most devices, plus attestation-backed tokens for managed/regulated customers.

Proposed flow (rough):
- Provisioning:
  - Device installs onboarding client. Exchanges an onboarding code (single-use) for a device id and initial refresh token. Provisioning happens out-of-band (email/manual, or org sync) depending on customer.
  - Server stores device metadata: device_id, public_key (optional), provisioning_tier (managed/unmanaged), last_seen.

- Normal auth flow:
  1) Device has access_token (exp ~5m) and refresh_token (longer life, e.g., 30d but single-use sliding).
  2) Device calls /v1/infer with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.
  3) Edge gateway validates JWT signature + scope + exp (fast local cache of public keys).
  4) If access_token expired -> device calls /v1/token/refresh with refresh_token and device_id. Server validates refresh token (rotate on use) and issues new access_token + new refresh_token.

- Refresh token rotation pattern:
  - Use one-time-use refresh tokens (rotate on each refresh). Keep a small grace window (one previously valid token) to tolerate concurrency.
  - Refresh token stored hashed server-side (like OAuth best practice).

- Public key distribution / caching:
  - Servers sign access tokens with rotating signing keys (K1, K2). Public keys published via /v1/keys and pushed to edge gateways via control plane. Gateways maintain cache with TTL.
  - Gateways should fetch new keys proactively and support key-id (kid) header in JWT.

- Offline device behavior:
  - If device is offline, allow local operation with cached access_token until it expires. For managed devices that need longer offline windows, support "offline-lease" tokens with explicit shorter scope (e.g., local-only inference) and constrained privileges.

API sketches (text):
- POST /v1/token/refresh\  request: { grant_type: "refresh_token", device_id: "dev-...", refresh_token: "xxx" }\  response: { access_token: "jwt..", expires_in: 300, refresh_token: "new-opaque", device_id: "dev-..." }

- GET /v1/keys\  response: { keys: [{ kid: "K1", alg: "RS256", pem: "---BEGIN PUBLIC---" }, ...] }

Sequence diagram (ascii):
Device -> Gateway -> Control Plane/Token Service\Device: call with access_token\Gateway: verify JWT (kid->local keys cache)\Gateway -> Token Service: if key missing or kid unknown -> fetch /v1/keys\Token Service: return keys\Gateway: accept/reject\Device: on 401 -> call refresh endpoint (POST /v1/token/refresh)\Token Service: validate (rotate refresh token) -> issue tokens

Key lifecycle notes:
- Signing keys: rotate on a schedule (e.g., 7d) but keep previous key for verification for 14d.
- Store private keys in KMS/HSM. Signing happens in confined signing service to make key rotation auditable.
- Public key must be served via a consistent URL and include metadata (created_at, expires_at).

Telemetry and attack detection:
- High refresh rates for a device -> mark suspicious.
- Failed refresh attempts -> increment device risk score, potentially throttle and require re-provisioning.
- Sudden geographic hop in last_seen -> alert for managed devices.

Edge gateway implementation notes:
- Gateways keep in-memory public-key cache with TTL (60s) and backoff on fetch failures.
- For each request, validate kid, signature, exp, scope. Cheap path: avoid network hop to token service in <99% cases.
- Provide a fast-path config toggle to allow local validation only for Dedicated deployments (customers with private control plane may prefer no external calls).

Security: revocation & emergency kills:
- Admin action to revoke device -> mark device_id revoked in DB and push revocation message to gateways via control plane.
- Gateways subscribe to streaming revocation feed (WebSocket/long-poll) and apply immediate deny for revoked device_ids present in incoming requests.
- For hosted API with many ephemeral gateways, keep a short TTL on access_tokens to minimize exposure.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Refresh token lifetime tradeoffs for unmanaged devices (30d vs 7d). Longer life increases risk but improves UX. Need metrics: average device offline duration by product.
- Support for certificate-based onboarding for large fleet customers (should we store device public key or an enrollment cert?).
- How to support on-prem agents that cannot reach control plane at all (air-gapped)? Probably need an explicit on-prem product path with manual key injection and longer offline leases.
- Rate-limit rules and graceful degradation: how many refreshes per minute per account before we throttle?

Testing plan (quick):
- Unit tests for token rotation logic, including concurrency where two refresh attempts race -> accept one and reject other with 401 and hint to re-run.
- Integration: gateway cache expiry tests, control plane key rotation tests.
- Chaos test: simulate signer unavailability and ensure gateways still accept tokens signed by previous keys until expiration window.

Action items (me):
- [ ] Pull device offline metrics from product analytics (ask Leah).
- [ ] Draft a minimal token RFC for review (include attestation options).
- [ ] Spike an in-memory one-time refresh token store with concurrent refresh test.

Notes-to-self: keep UX friction low for end users. Prefer server side defensible defaults and make the hard/secure paths opt-in for enterprise customers.

Questions for Marco on next sync:
- Do we want gateway-level revocation cache size bounds? (how many device_ids can be cached)
- Do we want per-customer configurable access_token TTL?

End.
